issue:
304 wrongly documented as following ErrorSchema
Automatic doc says 304 comes with a JSON payload. This is not true.

From https://httpstatuses.com/304:

> A 304 response cannot contain a message-body; it is always terminated by the first empty line after the header fields.

Flask/werkzeug respect that and 304 responses have an empty body.

Autodoc should be fixed.

We should clarify first which codes are concerned. There could be more than just 304 concerned.

Also, when `NotModified` is raised, we go through the error handler. This is useless since the payload is trashed. I don't think we should worry about that.

1  .. _etag:
   2  .. currentmodule:: flask_smorest
   3  
   4  ETag
   5  ====
   6  
   7  ETag is a web cache validation mechanism. It allows an API client to make
   8  conditional requests, such as
   9  
  10  - GET a resource unless it is the same as the version in cache.
  11  - PUT/PATCH/DELETE a resource unless the version in cache is outdated.
  12  
  13  The first case is mostly useful to limit the bandwidth usage, the latter
  14  addresses the case where two clients update a resource at the same time (known
  15  as the "*lost update problem*").
  16  
  17  The ETag featured is available through the
  18  :meth:`Blueprint.etag <Blueprint.etag>` decorator. It can be disabled globally
  19  with the `ETAG_DISABLED` application parameter.
  20  
  21  `flask-smorest` provides helpers to compute ETag, but ultimately, only the
  22  developer knows what data is relevant to use as ETag source, so there can be
  23  manual work involved.
  24  
  25  ETag Computed with API Response Data
  26  ------------------------------------
  27  
  28  The simplest case is when the ETag is computed using returned data, using the
  29  :class:`Schema <marshmallow.Schema>` that serializes the data.
  30  
  31  In this case, almost eveything is automatic. Only the call to
  32  :meth:`Blueprint.check_etag <Blueprint.check_etag>` is manual.
  33  
  34  The :class:`Schema <marshmallow.Schema>` must be provided explicitly, even
  35  though it is the same as the response schema.
  36  
  37  .. code-block:: python
  38      :emphasize-lines: 28,37
  39  
  40      @blp.route("/")
  41      class Pet(MethodView):
  42          @blp.etag
  43          @blp.response(200, PetSchema(many=True))
  44          def get(self):
  45              return Pet.get()
  46  
  47          @blp.etag
  48          @blp.arguments(PetSchema)
  49          @blp.response(201, PetSchema)
  50          def post(self, new_data):
  51              return Pet.create(**new_data)
  52
